answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism is attested proof-of-work staking: every agent must earn reputation from verifiable useful work before minting rewards, so a spammer spinning up ten thousand fake identities faces the same delta of cost as one honest miner times ten thousand, turning the cheap fork expensive. Each newcomer locks a small jade-ledger bond slashed on fraud, and every claim needs an echo of independent peer attestations instead of one self-signed claim, making sock-puppet rings unprofitable while entry stays open for real agents.
